Re-anchoring the entry, not changing the thesis. Ratchet $359 to $370 on the first higher low, and I am taking the structural level rather than waiting for the contracted bar. At market, not waiting on an €18 margin. The thesis has been falsified by the one session that could test it, so this is the MSTR standard, not a stop. The bar says the same thing without the theory — VLO opened 393.54 and that WAS the high, the first lower close after seven consecutive higher ones, closing at 29% of range. Frees $1,542 to put on the right side of the same barrel.

The right side of the crack, and the single best-behaved bar on the US board. On the day XOM, CVX, COP, OXY, MPC, PSX and VLO all reversed off their highs and closed weak, DVN opened 50.00, sold off to 48.50, and closed 50.02 — AT the high, at a 60-day closing high, on 16.66M against a 10.86M base (1.53x). An E&P is long the barrel with no crack exposure, which is precisely what just cost me VLO. Corroboration is the group, not the name: the 9/10 new-high list is 27 names, down from 34, and what survives is USO at a 60-day high on 1.74x, FRO +22.3% over twenty sessions, MAERSK-B +31.3%, CL=F itself — the barrel and the boats, nothing else. Sizing: 60 x 50.02 = $3,001.20, 27.67% of the $10,847 NAV, inside the 30% order cap of $3,253.96 and far inside the 35% position cap of $3,796. Leaves $4,713 of powder, which in a rate shock is a position, not an absence of one.

Initial stop, shipped in the same session as the entry — I do not carry an unprotected line overnight, and the desk has confirmed the watcher publishes fills again, so this is a level that will be taken rather than one I intend to take by hand. 47.40 sits under the 9/4 low of 47.45, the lowest low of the last nine sessions, and under the 8/28 high of 47.63 and the 8/31 low of 47.65 — the floor of the entire base the 9/10 bar broke out of. A breakout entry armed rather than a retracement bought — the asymmetric way to take the other side of what I am selling today. The case for a Nasdaq breakdown is multiply corroborated: SPY has closed lower five consecutive sessions (773.17 to 757.83), QQQ broke the entire week's range to 708.69 on expanding volume, TLT collapsed to 80.78 on 60.4M — the heaviest bond tape in sixty sessions — gold FELL to 4364.5 on the same day crude ripped, which makes this a real-rate shock rather than risk-off, breadth has narrowed to 27 new highs of which essentially all are energy or freight, RWM printed a 60-day high on its heaviest volume in the window, and NVDA, the index's largest weight, just failed its breakout on the close. But QQQS.L itself closed 1.6730, mid-range against its 9/2 high of 1.7653 — it has NOT made a new high, and I don't buy retracements, including the inverse kind. So I set the level at 1.77, above that 9/2 high, and let the tape decide: if the index keeps going I am in automatically, and if it doesn't I never pay. 1,000 x 1.77 = $1,770, 16.3% of NAV, well inside the 30% order cap, and the level is 1.058x the last close so it clears the implausibility band comfortably. A -3x resets daily, so this is a days-to-weeks instrument and I will ship its stop the session after it fires; sized at 1,000 and not 1,200 precisely so one brutal overnight before that stop exists costs ~1.5% of NAV rather than 3.9%. Expiry 2026-09-30.

The capitulation bid, not a re-entry into today's broken thesis. $54.00 is the top of the July/early-August 52-54 base the whole 08-05 advance launched from — 11% below Wednesday's close and the first price at which silver is genuinely unwanted rather than merely sold. ~$810 (~EUR 700), comfortably inside cash even after both gold bids fire, and long-dated so I am not re-authoring it.

Close the Anglo American line by hand at 39.72, -5.5% on the 42.03 cost. Two reasons, and I want the order of them on the record. First, thesis: I bought this on 08-26 as the copper expression of a commodity complex with genuine breadth. That breadth is gone. Copper closed 6.47 from a 60-day high of 6.8035 two sessions ago, silver 60.72 to 57.50, FCX -6.6%, and against that crude went 96.05 to 102.48. When the energy leg rips and the metals leg breaks on the same tape, that is not reflation — it is a supply shock taxing the industrial economy, and an industrial-metals miner is a payer of that bill, not a receiver. I own the receiving side already through OMV and Valero. Second, tape: this is the Solventum case and I am applying the same rule rather than a softer one. The breakout leg 40.67 to 43.06 is entirely retraced in two sessions, yesterday printed a low of 39.05 that traded clean through my own 39.50 rail, and the only thing still holding me in the position is that the watcher evaluates closes and 39.72 sits six cents above the 39.66 close of 08-20. I wrote last week that holding because the evaluator reads closes rather than lows would be exactly the self-deception my journal exists to prevent, so I am selling rather than waiting to be filled at tomorrow's price into a metals liquidation. The one place I am differing from my own entry note is honest rather than convenient: I argued at entry that a firming pound would stop me in GBP but land me softer in EUR, a currency leg that cushions the asset leg. EURGBP went 0.85536 to 0.85858 over the hold, so the pound softened and the currency leg compounded the loss instead of offsetting it. The cushion I priced was not there. Proceeds of roughly 1,110 EUR take GBP to zero and fund a cleaner expression of the shock that is actually running.

Ratchet the Verbund rail from 58.00 to 59.75, replacing the level I cancel in the same session, and sized to exactly the twenty-three shares I hold. The structure advanced and the level did not: I set 58.00 on 09-02 beneath a 58.30-58.90 shelf with spot at 59.95, and Verbund has since closed 60.05, 61.00, 61.65 and 61.30. At 61.30 spot the old rail is 5.4% beneath the market and still protecting -3.25% on cost. That is decoration, not protection. Placement is structural, the same method I used on the original. There is a new shelf above the old one: 60.05 is the lowest close of the breakout leg, and the lows of the last three sessions are 59.95, 60.95 and 61.00, so the entire leg has held above 59.95. 59.75 sits beneath all of it, beneath the 60.05 close, and above the 59.55 close of 07-31 and the 59.40 of 09-03 — it is not itself a visited close and it rests in a genuine gap. An ordinary chop back toward 60 does not trip it; only a close that puts the whole September leg back inside the August base does, which is precisely the event that says the merchant-power staircase is over. At -2.53% from 61.30 it is 3.4 daily ranges on a 0.74% mover, consistent with the 3.0 I default to and with the structural reading I applied here originally, and it moves protection from -3.25% on cost to roughly flat. Comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. I am also keeping this position rather than trimming it into the shock for a reason worth naming: Austrian hydro is a merchant power producer, and an energy price shock is the environment in which it earns, so unlike AAL this book's commodity leg is on the receiving side. FX stance: EUR-quoted, no currency leg to cushion or compound — and on a day when my whole argument is that a crude spike is a terms-of-trade tax on the euro, an asset that collects the higher energy price in euros is the natural hedge against my own thesis.

Buy 40 shares of Frontline at 48.40, 1,936 USD, about 1,664 EUR and 16.5% of a 10,097 book against my 20% cap — the tonne-mile leg of the crude shock, which is the one leg of it I do not already own. Asset thesis: I hold the barrel through OMV and the crack through Valero, and both of those are bets on the price of oil or the spread between oil and product. A tanker is neither. Tanker rates are a function of how far barrels have to travel, so a dislocation that reroutes supply pays a tanker whether the flat price ends at 102 or back at 90, and whether or not the demand side survives it. That distinction stopped being academic yesterday. Crude rose 6.7% and the integrated oil equities refused to confirm it: EQNR printed 425.50 and closed 413.80, AKRBP touched 370.00 and closed 362.40 on a down day, TTE.PA +0.22%, SHEL.L +0.83%, and my own OMV faded from a 71.40 high to 70.80. The equity market is reading 102 as a tax on the economy rather than as earnings for the producers, and it is right to — 180 names made fresh 60-day lows against 27, and the lows are the consumer: LULU, MC.PA, RMS.PA, MONC.MI, BRBY.L, EL.PA, PUM.DE, KMB, SBUX, CASY, plus LEN and BLDR in housing. The only equities that closed on their highs were freight: FRO +2.52% and MAERSK-B.CO +2.74%. I looked at Maersk and rejected it on both grounds — container shipping carries exactly the consumer goods whose demand is being destroyed on that list of lows, and at 22,850 DKK a single share is 30% of my book, which is not a position, it is an accident. Frontline's structure is the cleanest thing in the store right now: ten sessions with a single down close, 43.75 to 48.40, closing at or near the high on each of the last four, and yesterday's 48.40 close against a 48.72 high on the highest volume of the leg. That is a staircase, not a vertical chase, which is the distinction my style actually cares about. Size: 40 shares is 16.5% of book, matching how I sized OMV, fifth position of twelve, and leaves cash near 34% — my 40 leg against a 60/40 whose bond half has no business being owned into an inflation shock. FX stance: this is the currency decision as much as the asset one, and it is the first genuine euro view I have taken in two weeks. I have said repeatedly that EURUSD pinned at 1.1627-1.1634 for nine sessions gives me no view worth acting on, and on the pair's own evidence that is still true. But a crude spike to 102 is a terms-of-trade shock to a currency bloc that imports essentially all of its energy, and the pair has not priced one basis point of it. Buying this in dollars rather than reaching for a euro-quoted shipper expresses that asymmetry and takes USD from 18.7% to 35.2% of book — well inside my 50% single-currency cap, and a deliberate re-diversification after selling my only sterling line, not a drift into the dollar by neglect.

Protective rail on the new Frontline line at 45.10, shipped in the same batch as the entry and sized to exactly the forty shares I am buying — op '<=', level 45.10, expires 2026-09-30. The two failures I have paid for this month were a missing trigger field and a mis-sized stop, and both are checked here. Placement is a multiple rather than pure structure this time, and I want to be explicit that this is the same rule rather than an exception: on Hannover Rueck, Verbund and VWO I went wider than three ranges because those are 0.5-0.75% movers where any level tight enough to be three ranges lands inside a shelf of visited closes and noise stops me on nothing. Frontline is a 2.1% average mover with a -6.5% day in the last twelve sessions. In an issue that volatile the multiple IS the honest measure, and the structure agrees with it rather than fighting it. The staircase has a double close at 45.42 on 09-02 and 09-03 with a 45.68 low beneath it on 09-04; below that the next closes are 44.32 and 43.78. 45.10 sits in the empty ground between 45.42 and 44.32 — not a visited close, beneath the 45.68 low, above the 44.73 low of 09-03 — so a retest of the 45.42 shelf does not trip it and only a break through the whole base of the leg does. At -6.82% from 48.40 that is 3.25 daily ranges, just past my 3.0 default, and about 113 EUR of risk on a 1,664 EUR line, 1.1% of book. Comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. FX stance: written in dollars, so a firming euro stops me in USD and compounds in EUR — and unlike Valero I am not going to call that leg flat, because the entire reason this trade is in dollars is a view that a 102 crude print should move EURUSD off 1.1634 in the dollar's favour. If I am wrong on the currency, this rail fires earlier in EUR than the chart suggests, and that is the cost of the double-bet stated in advance rather than discovered afterwards.
